lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Percentages
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 6, Session 3
lesson.footer: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 3

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Years 5 and 6: connecting percentages with fractions and decimals (out of 100), using multiplication and division to make equivalent fractions
plan.shape: example-first on a hundred grid, then a table of all three names, because 'out of 100' is the bridge between them
plan.criticalFeature: per cent means out of 100: make the fraction out of 100 and you have the percentage
decisionPoints: the choice check: which grid shows 7%?
plan.anchor: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Shade 45 squares on a hundred grid: 45/100 = 0.45. Today adds the third name: 45%.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Shade and name hundred grids, a three-names table, a mistake, and sport and shopping percentages.
resources.title: Percentages
resources.subtitle: Per cent means out of 100.

example.prompt: Name the shaded part three ways.

items.prompt: Write the shaded part as a decimal.
Shade 70%. Write it as a decimal.

example.prompt: Write 3/5 as a decimal and a percentage.
A team won 15 of 25 games. What percentage did they win?

items.prompt: A shooter scored 18 of 20 goals. What percentage is that?
In a class of 25, 7 walk to school. What percentage walk?
Jack wrote 0.5 as a percentage. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: 0.5 is 5 tenths = 50 hundredths, so it is 50%.

items.prompt: Which is the biggest share of a pizza?

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Percentages over 100%, halves of a percent, and a design task, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Tricky Percentages
resources.subtitle: Over 100% and less than 1%.

items.prompt: A footy crowd was 120% of last week's. What does that mean?
items.answer: It was bigger than last week's: last week's crowd plus another 20% of it.

items.prompt: Write 12.5% as a fraction in simplest form.

example.prompt: Colour a flag that is 40% blue.

items.prompt: Design a team flag on a 10 by 10 grid that is 35% red, 0.4 blue and the rest white. What percentage is white? Show your working.
items.answer: 35 red squares, 40 blue squares, 25 white squares: 25% white.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: hundred grids to count, a three-names frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Percentages: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Count the shaded squares out of 100.

slides.notes: Session 3 of our fractions, decimals and percentages week: today we meet the third name, percentages.
Before you start, put boards, markers and coloured pencils on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Fair or not?
prompts: Spinner: half red, a quarter blue, a quarter green. Red wins for Ali, blue or green for Bo. Fair?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with probability, coordinates and area.
ASK: Is this spinner game fair?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: fair, 1/2 each
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> write each player's chance: Ali half, Bo a quarter plus a quarter. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Fair: Ali has a half, and Bo has two quarters,
also a half. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying unfair because Bo has two colours.
Fix: add Bo's chances, and they compare again.
notes.prep: Review of Week 4 probability (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Missing corner
prompts: What are the coordinates of the fourth corner D?

beats: ASK: What are the coordinates of the fourth corner, D?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (1, 5)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> trace up from A and across from C together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 1, 5: above A, level with C. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (5, 1).
Fix: say the anchor, across first, and they rewrite it.

slides.title: Composite area
prompts: Find the area of the L-shape.

beats: ASK: What is the area of this L-shape?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 52 m²
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> draw the split line, then find each rectangle's area. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The bottom is 10 by 4, 40, and the top is 4 by 3,
12: 52 square metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: multiplying the two longest sides.
Fix: shade the missing corner, and they split it.

beats: SAY: Now for our eight times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 8 times 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 64
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double, double, double: 16, 32, 64. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 64. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 56 or 72.
Fix: double 8 three times: 16, 32, 64, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 8 times 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 32
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 4, then again, then again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 32. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 24 or 36.
Fix: double 4 three times: 8, 16, 32, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many eights make 96?
ASK: What is 96 divided by 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> 10 eights is 80, then 2 more eights. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 11.
Fix: check: 12 eights is 96, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to write percentages as fractions and decimals, and back again.
successCriteria: I can say what per cent means: out of 100.
I can write the same amount as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
I can explain which name is easiest to use in a real situation.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We've switched between fractions and decimals.
Today we add the third name: the percentage.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 out of 100 is reachable for everyone; SC2 three names is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 choosing a name is the stretch.

notes.answer: 80 out of 100: most of the battery is left
beats: POINT to each picture.
SAY: Some of you may see percentages every day:
your device battery, sales in shops, test scores.
ASK: What do you think 80 percent battery means? Tell your partner.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: 80 out of 100, most of it is charged
SAY: 80 percent means 80 out of 100, so most of the battery is left.
Per cent means out of 100. Today we connect it to fractions and decimals.
trap: thinking 80% means 80 minutes.
Fix: say per cent means out of 100, and they explain again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: everyday percentages. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A number out of 100, written with the % sign.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is percentage. Say it with me: per-cent-age.
SAY: Per cent means out of 100. 45 percent means 45 out of every 100.
We write it with the per cent sign.
ASK: What does 100 percent mean?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the whole: 100 out of 100
trap: saying 100% is a lot but not all.
Fix: shade all 100 squares, and they say it again.
notes.prep: Per cent: per = for each, cent = 100.

beats: POINT to the grid.
SAY: 37 of the 100 squares are shaded. That's 37 out of 100.
MODEL the three names.
SAY: As a fraction, 37/100. As a decimal, 0.37.
And because it's out of 100, it's 37 percent.
ASK: If 8 squares were shaded, what would the three names be?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 8/100, 0.08 and 8 percent.
Out of 100 links all three.
trap: writing 0.8 for 8%.
Fix: write it into the place value chart as hundredths, and they fix it.
notes.stretch: Write 80% three ways. How is it different from 8%?
notes.help: Count the shaded squares, then write 'out of 100'.
notes.prep: Out of 100 is the bridge: the critical feature. SC1 and SC2.

beats: POINT to the bar.
SAY: To change 7/20 into a percentage, I need it out of 100.
20 times 5 is 100, so I multiply the top and bottom by 5.
MODEL 7 times 5.
SAY: 7 times 5 is 35, so 7/20 is 35/100, which is 35 percent.
ASK: Now you try: how would you write 9/25 as a percentage?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 36%
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 25 times 4 is 100, and 9 times 4 is 36: 36 percent.
trap: writing 9% or 25%.
Fix: ask what times 25 makes 100, and they multiply.
notes.help: List the times table of the denominator up to 100.
notes.prep: Same move as Session 1, new name. SC2.

slides.title: Which grid shows 7%?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: shades by guessing, not counting out of 100

beats: SAY: Count carefully: per cent means out of 100.
ASK: Which grid shows 7 percent?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What percentage is A?
Less -> count 7 squares on the board grid together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B: 7 squares out of 100.
A is 70 percent, 7 full rows.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: count A's squares, 70, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: 7% confused with 0.7 or 70%.

slides.title: Switch the name
slides.ask: Write it in the form asked for.
slides.pivot: make it out of 100 first, then read the percentage
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you make it out of 100?

say: Write each answer on your board.
trap: writing 0.6 as 6%.
Fix: say 6 tenths is 60 hundredths, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write each answer in the third form too.
notes.help: Use the hundred grid to picture each amount.
notes.prep: Guided practice: benchmark, tenths, simplifying, a zero place holder and twentieths. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Make it out of 100 first.
ASK: How do you write 3/20 as a percentage?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 15%
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> ask what times 20 makes 100, then multiply the top. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Times 5: 15 out of 100, so 15 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 3%.
Fix: say twentieths are not hundredths, and they multiply.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing 3% or 20% starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Switch between fractions, decimals and percentages on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: How did you make it out of 100?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: writing tenths as single-digit percentages.
Fix: shade it on a hundred grid, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Extension: percentages over 100%, parts of a percent and designing a flag.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: hundred grids to count and a three-names frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: grids, a three-names table, a mistake and real percentages. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Write 0.4 as a fraction in simplest form, and as a percentage.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: How do you write 0.4 as a fraction in simplest form,
and as a percentage?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/5 and 40%
RECORD who writes 4% or 4/100.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 4%.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: both other names from a decimal.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner what per cent means, with an example.

notes.answer: open - listen for out of 100, like 45% is 45 out of 100
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can switch between all three names?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 4% on the board matters most.
ASK: What does per cent mean? Give an example.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: out of 100, like 45% is 45 out of 100
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: comparing and ordering.
